MINUTES
  Regular Meeting Notice of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, June 14, 2022

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:02 PM on Tuesday, June 14, 2022, Mayor Tasha Cerda
presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney
  Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

  At 7:03 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with the
  following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council
  Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present: City Attorney Carmen Vasquez.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION

  2.A  Public Employee Performance Evaluation
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager

  Mayor Cerda reconvened the meeting to the Regular Open Session at 7:53
  p.m., and the City Clerk noted the return of all Council Members, who were
  present at the meeting. When City Attorney Vasquez was asked if there was
  any reportable action from Closed Session, she stated that staff was
  provided with direction, but no reportable action had been taken.

3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Damilola "Dami" Ogundimu and Abisola "Abi" Ogundimu led the Pledge of Allegiance. Both
  Dami and Abi attend Chadwick School. Today we have a duo, two sisters who have been
  residents of Gardena for ten years. They are committed to the City and passionate about
  giving back and providing service. They have just begun their quest on community service
  by assisting with Kid's to Park Day we had in May and will be volunteering for Flag Day and
  Juneteenth. So be on the lookout for these two. They are our future leaders for the City.

4.  INVOCATION

  Presented by Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka

  emergency regulations.

  what the city and residents will be required to do during the drought.

directly to Zoom and entering the Meeting ID: 813 7129 8336 and or calling in with Phone number

15.B Approve Four-Year Contract for Citywide Tree Trimming Maintenance Service
  Contract to Mariposa Landscapes Inc. in the amount of $480,472.02

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Kaskanian had questions regarding the new contract and expressed
  in detail how he felt about the service the City received from West Coast Arborist; he
  continued to say it was not adequate for the money we paid. Council Member Francis
  asked about the number of trees that were being serviced and asked if park trees
  were included; she then asked if staff could do the work, and who is doing the work
  now. Mayor Cerda asked if the vendor had a back-up plan in the event their
  equipment broke and talked about the complaints.

  Director of Public Works, Allan Rigg came into the meeting and gave history
  regarding the past work and he spoke about his plan to start a more aggressive tree
  planting program and manage the new contract more diligently, he then stated if they
  didn’t perform to our satisfaction that we would be able to terminate the contract and
  then asked City Attorney Vasquez to speak on the non-performance clause; City
  Attorney Vasquez replied that with regards to non-performance, we would have to
  give them the opportunity to cure the issue, before we could terminate the contract.

  Public Speakers: Zahid Ahmed, Abel Ruan, and Wanda Love spoke on this topic,
  voiced their concerns and offered ideas.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Award Tree Trimming
  Maintenance Service Contract:

  Ayes:  Council Member Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka and Mayor Cerda

15.D PUBLIC HEARING: RESOLUTION NO. 6582, Approving a Franchise Fee, an AB
  939/SB 1383 Fee, and Residential and Commercial Solid Waste Disposal and
  Recycling Rates Effective July 1, 2022

  RESOLUTION NO. 6582

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A FRANCHISE FEE, AN AB
  939/SB 1383 FEE AND RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SOLID
  WASTE DISPOSAL AND RECYCLING RATES EFFECTIVE JULY 1,
  2022

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Consultant Debbie Morris, WRG representatives, Bevan Thomas and Michelle
  Nichols were present and available for any questions.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 10:12 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  Public Speakers: Hopeton Hutchinson; Abel Ruan; Wanda Love; Judy Kim and
  Zahid Ahmed spoke in protest of this item.

  There was discussion that included Mayor Cerda, Council Member Francis, City
  Attorney Vasquez and WRG representative Bevan Thomas regarding the types of
  items that could go into a dumpster, the number of protests that would need to be
  collected in order for the rates to not be approved; who was allowed to protest; why
  the increase is necessary now.

  Director Rigg came into the meeting and spoke about the conditions in the contract
  and how the residents of Gardena would benefit; some of the benefits included a
  spring cleaning to happen every six months; bulky item pickup two times a year; an
  annual compost giveaway; and an annual document shredding event. He continued
  to say that the contract did not offer a senior discount and that our rates are right in
  the middle when compared to other cities; and our commercial rates are slightly
  8
   higher than the average. Attorney Vasquez confirmed that in order for the rates to
  not be approved, we would have had to receive 50% plus 1 protests from the
  property owners or customer of record; she also indicated that parcel owners or
  customer of record were the only ones allowed to make a protest; she then stated
  that our contract was up for renewal and since we had additional state laws with the
  organic waste that were recently passed, and an additional service was required,
  we had a little more leverage since our contract was about to expire. She
  commended Consultant Debbie Morris and Director Rigg for the great negotiation
  they provided to the City in the positive rates for our residents. She then stated that
  we had no control over the commercial rates since the state was adding this service
  but not giving us any funding.

  Deputy City Clerk Romero read into the record the amount of written protest received
  which was 14.

  There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 10:40 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Kaskanian, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Conduct Public Hearing
  and Adopt Resolution No. 6582:

  Ayes:  Council Member Kaskanian, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members
  Henderson and Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

  12

3. COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS – Since the last meeting Council Member Francis

  Member Francis is a trustee at the Greater Los Angeles Vector Control District. She also
  shared that June 19th through June 25th is National Mosquito Control Week and since it’s

  mentioned in the next City Council Meeting there will be a presentation, and if anyone
  has questions or would like more information, they can go to mosquitowatch.org.
